The remaining sentence of Section 16 of EO 11001 revokes Emergency Preparedness Orders Nos. 4 and 5, issued earlier by the Director of the Office of Civil and Defense Mobilization. The revocation was a one-time act performed when the President signed the order on February 16, 1962; the order states no later effective date, so the command was exhausted by performance on that date. Its consequence, that the earlier issuance was revoked, survives separately from the order's continuing commands, and nothing in the held text of EO 11490 sections 3011 to 3015 revives it. The source cited for the date is this order's own text.

research_rationale:
EO 11001 (1962-02-16; Assigning emergency preparedness functions to the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare): the held Federal Register text was checked against its heading, numbered sections and closing date, and searched for expiry, "until", termination and effective-date wording. The order assigns continuing emergency preparedness planning functions and its own terms contain no end date or end condition. The end is EO 11490 of October 28, 1969, whose Sec. 3015 revokes the order by number; the end source is the American Presidency Project transcription of EO 11490 (APP node 255823, Common Crawl capture 2025-11-18T01:11:34Z), whose Sec. 3015 list agrees with the Federal Register text of 34 FR 17567 onward (issue of October 30, 1969) read for corroboration. The held texts citing this order's number were searched with the repository number lookup and no earlier revocation or supersession was found. The order also revoked earlier issuances by its own closing sentence where one is stated, a one-time act recorded as a separate scope. The legal cutoff is 2026-10-14; no continuing predicate is needed for a NO order.

savings.reason: No provision of EO 11490 sections 3011 to 3015, the span quoted as the end source, preserves EO 11001 after its revocation; section 3014 retains existing assignments only "Except as provided in Section 3015". The completed revocation of any earlier emergency preparedness or mobilization order stays effective as a spent act. I did not search the remainder of EO 11490 for successor assignments to the same agency, so no transfer of this order's commands is claimed.
